name: The Holy Innocents
history: The children of Bethlehem killed by King Herod in his attempt to destroy the newborn Christ. The Church honours them as martyrs, who confessed Christ not by speaking but by dying.
meditation: Pray today for children who suffer, born and unborn.
life: Saint Matthew's Gospel tells that when the Magi did not return, King Herod, furious, ordered the killing of all the boys in Bethlehem and its district who were two years old or under, and that Joseph had already taken the Child and His mother to Egypt. Matthew sees in this the fulfilment of Jeremiah's words about Rachel weeping for her children. The deed fits what is known of Herod, who killed a wife and several of his own sons. Bethlehem was a small town, and the number of children was probably small, but each was a child known and loved. The Church has kept their feast since the fifth century, and they are honoured as martyrs who died not only for Christ but in His place. In England the day was once called Childermas.
prayerTo: Holy Innocents, little ones of Bethlehem, you gave your lives before you could speak His name. Pray for children who suffer violence, neglect or hunger, for children who have died, and for their grieving parents. Pray for all who hold power over the weak, that they may protect the smallest and most defenceless. Amen.
penance: Give to a charity that protects children, and pray today for parents who have lost a child.
prayer: O God, Whose praise the Innocents, Your martyrs, this day proclaimed, not by speaking, but by dying, put to death in us all the wickedness of sin, so that Your faith which our tongue professes may be proclaimed also by our life. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
